name: fix105_torch
verifies: fix-105 (owner, Demo_2026-10-18c: the torch could no longer be taken into the hand from the quick slot or the inventory): the torch's quick-slot key takes it into the left hand and puts it away again (G3 _AI_HoldLeftInventoryItem); with a one-handed weapon drawn it is taken beside it; a bow drawn from its quick slot takes the left hand (the torch goes back into the inventory) and the torch's key with the bow drawn does not take it; after the bow is put away it is taken again; and when a hero bone is destroyed after the overlay masks were built (the MetaHuman head swap: G3MotionPlayer.MaskFor threw a NullReferenceException and HeroTorchView waited for an overlay that never started) the keys still work
steps: log -- on and off from the quick slot
log -- beside a drawn one-handed weapon
log -- the bow takes the left hand
log -- a hero bone lost after the overlay masks were built (the MetaHuman head swap)
notes: quickslot presses the slot's key through QuickSlotInput.Use, the player's path (PlayerCombat.TryReady first: weapons and spells; then HeroItemUse.UseQuickSlot -> HeroTorchView.TryUse). torch = the torch item in the left hand ('-' none), torchbusy = its take/put-away overlay runs, torchfails = takes/put-aways whose motion threw (HeroTorchView finishes them at once; must stay 0: with the old MaskFor the bone part threw here). Owner's Player-prev.log: NullReferenceException in G3MotionPlayer.MaskFor (Transform.IsChildOf / name on a destroyed bone) from HeroTorchView.NextPart <- TryUse <- QuickSlotInput, and from G3CombatAnimator.PlayOverlayStep <- Aim. Since fix-110 MaskFor rebuilds its bone list when one was destroyed (the same root cause, found for spells), and since fix-105 the torch view gives up an overlay that threw or ran past 3 s.
